newsitem.title: UK: Virgin considers UK-Far East cargo flights.
newsitem.headline: Virgin considers UK-Far East cargo flights.

text.p: Virgin Atlantic Airways is considering launching regular freighter flights between the UK and an unnamed Far Eastern destination with wet-leased aircraft later this year, said its cargo general manager commercial, David Woodward.

"A freighter proposal is currently on the table and its viability is being evaluated," he told Reuters, adding that if the go-ahead were given, a Boeing 747F or MD-11 freighter would be used, wet-leased from a specialist operator.
"It must revolve around commercial demand. The be all and end all is commercial viability," he said.
"I believe the demand is there (for a freighter operation), as is the revenue to sustain it," he said.
Wet leasing covers the hire of both aircraft and crew and these arrangements also usually cover maintenance and insurance.

Woodward declined to name the proposed destination but said that Virgin's current Asian routes -- from London Heathrow to Tokyo and Hong Kong -- were attracting good bellyhold cargo traffic and yields, particularly to and from Japan.

"For Virgin, London-Tokyo, on which we operate six Airbus A340 flights a week, is a consistent all-year round cargo performer. Our yields on the route are excellent, up 4.3 percent so far this year (on the same period in 1996) based on just about the same tonnage flown," he said.
"The strength of the pound against the yen and the recent rise in Japan's consumption tax have had no detrimental effect on our business," Woodward added.

He described London-Hong Kong as "a good market" but said its growth for Virgin Cargo was being hampered by "inconsistent uplift in both directions" caused by restricted aircraft performance on a long, diverse routeing.

Two years ago, Virgin Atlantic Cargo disclosed it had had preliminary talks with Federal Express about starting a possible joint UK-Hong Kong freighter service, but Woodward said that nothing had come of these.

Commenting on the new proposal, he said that Virgin's possible entry into the freighter business would "not be aimed just at obtaining further market share or relieving (space) pressure in the market".

Woodward added if Virgin did decide to proceed with the freighter venture, it would go out to win traffic from the heavy freight sector of the market as well as the smaller and medium-sized shipments already carried on its passenger aircraft.
